newsitem.title: GERMANY: Court releases two in German kidnap case.
newsitem.headline: Court releases two in German kidnap case.

text.p: A German court on Thursday released two of five people detained on Wednesday in connection with the kidnapping of Frankfurt businessman Jakub Fiszman, prosecutors said.
Prosecutor Rainer Schilling said three further suspects would go before a judge on Thursday evening and prosecutors would apply to have them formally placed under arrest.

Schilling said a woman and a man had been released because there was not a sufficiently strong suspicion they were directly involved in the crime. The three people remaining in custody were a married couple and their 26-year-old son, he said.
Fiszman was abducted outside his Frankfurt office on October 1. The only sign of life since then has been a telephone call he made the next day to a woman friend.
Fiszman's brother Georg paid a ransom of four million marks ($2.6 million) on October 10, but his kidnappers reneged on an agreement and failed to free him the following day.
Police recovered most of the ransom on Wednesday in the garden of a flat in Wiesbaden, after searching several properties in the Frankfurt area and detaining the five suspects.
